name: Frontend Design
description: Give your interfaces a distinct point of view. Better typography, intentional layouts, and design that feels considered.
install: npx skills add anthropics/skills --skill frontend-design --agent codex

benefits: Choose a coherent visual direction before writing code.
Improve typography, spacing, motion, and responsive composition.
Keep the result grounded in your product rather than a template.
steps: Review the skill instructions and source.
Use Add to Codex to download the skill into this project’s .agents/skills folder.
On your next Codex turn, invoke $frontend-design with a specific brief.
Review the result at desktop and mobile sizes, including reduced motion.
guide.example: $frontend-design Build a personal AI capability observatory. Use graphite surfaces, a capability constellation, clear source status, and thoughtful interactions.
guide.caveat: A skill supplies instructions; it is not a trained model or a guarantee of design quality.

name: React Best Practices
description: Build faster React experiences with practical patterns for rendering, data fetching, and bundle performance.
install: npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill vercel-react-best-practices --agent codex

benefits: Find unnecessary rendering and expensive client work.
Review loading waterfalls and bundle size.
Turn performance advice into specific, reviewable changes.
steps: Read the source and choose a target component.
Add the skill to this project.
Ask Codex to inspect before editing.
Measure before and after with your profiler or build output.
guide.example: $vercel-react-best-practices Review my dashboard for rendering bottlenecks and request waterfalls. Explain the findings, then make the smallest useful fixes.
guide.caveat: Advice depends on your framework and version. Verify improvements with measurements.

name: Context7
description: Bring current library documentation and version-specific examples into your coding conversations.

benefits: Retrieve documentation close to the library version you use.
Give your agent examples grounded in a documented API.
Reduce guesses about unfamiliar or changing dependencies.
steps: Read the provider setup guide and authentication requirements.
Copy the MCP command into your terminal.
Check codex mcp list and complete any provider authentication.
Ask Codex to use Context7 for a specific library and version.
guide.example: Use Context7 to check the current Motion for React documentation, then implement an accessible expandable panel in my app.
guide.caveat: This connection may require provider credentials and has its own limits. Arnyx does not claim it is connected merely because it is cataloged.

name: Playwright MCP
description: Let your agent explore a real browser, follow user journeys, and inspect what actually appears on screen.

benefits: Exercise complete user journeys in a browser.
Inspect accessible page structure.
Reproduce UI bugs against the running app.
steps: Review the Microsoft repository and browser requirements.
Register the server with the copied command.
Run your app and check codex mcp list.
Ask Codex to exercise a clearly described journey.
guide.example: Use Playwright to open http://localhost:5175, filter skills by Design, open a walkthrough, and check the page at a mobile viewport.
guide.caveat: The browser can access sites and local pages. Keep sign-in and sensitive workflows under your control.

name: Web Design Guidelines
description: A practical second pair of eyes for accessibility, interaction patterns, and the details that make a site easier to use.
install: npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill web-design-guidelines --agent codex

benefits: Review keyboard, focus, and semantic controls.
Find common interaction and accessibility gaps.
Prioritize concrete fixes rather than visual opinions.
steps: Add the skill to your project.
Choose the pages or components you want reviewed.
Invoke $web-design-guidelines with that scope.
Verify findings in the browser and apply relevant fixes.
guide.example: $web-design-guidelines Review the discovery page for keyboard navigation, accessible dialogs, readable contrast, and reduced-motion behavior.
guide.caveat: An automated review is a starting point. Check with assistive technology where it matters.

name: GitHub MCP Server
description: Give your agent repository context: issues, pull requests, source files, and development workflows.

benefits: Bring repository and issue context into a task.
Review pull requests with their surrounding history.
Reduce switching between your editor and GitHub.
steps: Review the official server documentation and access requirements.
Configure the authentication method documented by GitHub.
Register the MCP server and verify codex mcp list.
Start with a read-only repository question.
guide.example: Using GitHub, summarize the open issues in my repository and identify the ones related to frontend performance. Do not change any issues.
guide.caveat: Authentication and plan requirements depend on GitHub. The endpoint command alone does not grant access.

name: Codex CLI
description: Your local coding agent, and the engine behind Arnyx’s coordinator. Reuse your existing CLI configuration and sign-in.

benefits: Work with local files and your existing tools.
Run repeatable tasks with structured JSON events.
Use one coordinator for the catalog, crawler activity, and your saved stack.
steps: Install the official Codex CLI if it is not already available.
Run codex login in your terminal.
Open Arnyx settings and verify the CLI connection.
Ask the coordinator about your stack or a discovery result.
guide.example: Compare the design skills in my Arnyx catalog. Recommend a small stack for building and testing a React dashboard, and explain the tradeoffs.
guide.caveat: Arnyx invokes codex exec in a read-only sandbox. CLI account limits and your selected provider still apply.

name: Knowledge Work Plugins
description: Explore reusable knowledge-work workflows for research, product work, and organization.

benefits: Discover focused workflows and reusable prompt patterns.
Learn how plugins combine instructions and tools.
Identify parts that can be adapted into Codex skills.
steps: Read the source repository and supported host information.
Choose one workflow and inspect its required tools.
Adapt compatible instructions into a Codex skill if licensing allows.
Configure corresponding MCP tools separately and test the workflow.
guide.example: Review this plugin workflow and explain which instructions could become a Codex skill, which tools need MCP equivalents, and which parts are unsupported.
guide.caveat: These plugins target another host. Arnyx does not automatically install them into Codex or claim host compatibility.
